title: FF Mark weight and letterform specimen
slide_intent: Expose the letterforms because a typeface should extend the visual character of the symbol while supporting a range of emphasis.
strategic_value: Circular letter structures can reinforce identity across text that carries no logo.
demonstration: A white FF Mark heading and repeated lowercase letter groups show thin-to-heavy weights on black.
practical_value: Compare rounded forms and weight changes without treating the specimen as a complete typographic scale.

content_islands.name: Family name
content_islands.spec: Set the white FF Mark title above the specimen.

content_islands.name: Letter groups
content_islands.spec: Arrange repeated a, m, r, t, s, e, d and c forms in staggered rows, progressing through weights.

reference_purposes.Expression: The specimen exposes rounded lowercase forms across a visible range of weights.
reference_purposes.Intent: Pentagram explains that FF Mark echoes the circular structure of the logo and references the 1979 typography.

ingredient.name: FF Mark
ingredient.role: Extend the circular identity into written messages.
ingredient.application: Use the published rounded letterforms and weight range as evidence of type character; this specimen supplies no size or spacing rules.
ingredient.scope: Historical 2016 Pentagram case study; not a current master guideline or numeric production specification.
